Hi team,

Thanks for taking a close look at the private offer we built for Acme. I attached a concise term sheet that maps the pricing tiers to buyer approval gates we discussed on the call last week. A few things I wanted to call out up front: 

- We can offer a 12‑month annual commit or a 24‑month discounted option (10% additional credit) depending on your buyer authorization window.
- For multi-division buyers, AWS requires each purchasing entity to be enumerated; we can put the additional divisions on an addendum rather than re-issuing a new PO.
- We can enable an escrow-style holdback on a modest portion of the committed spend for the first 90 days if that helps procurement mitigate onboarding risk.

Attached: Acme_PO_Term_Sheet.pdf (summary of pricing/terms) and redwood-private-offer-summary.xlsx (usage projections + cost model).

Next steps I suggest: 1) confirm which term length (12 vs 24 months) you prefer, 2) confirm the buyer entity list, and 3) tell me if the holdback/escrow is required by your finance/legal team — we can map the mechanics and draft language.

Happy to jump on a short call if that helps.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

Thanks Maria + Jordan —

Responses inline: 

1) Holdback/admin: AWS Marketplace supports seller escrow-style capabilities via the private offer process (seller-controlled holdback with explicit release criteria). Practically, Redwood can operate the holdback but we can include language that AWS will release funds to Redwood upon mutual confirmation of onboarding milestones. If Acme prefers a neutral third party, we can add an escrow agent clause and route via AWS Marketplace procurement options — that'll add a small admin step but is doable.

2) Early termination: For the 24-month option we propose a 90-day termination notice with a pro‑rata final settlement plus an early termination fee equal to 10% of remaining committed net spend. For 12-month contracts the termination notice is 60 days with a 5% remaining-commit fee. These are negotiable, but we included them to protect reserved capacity economics.

3) Multi-division pooling: We can structure the private offer as pooled (single account-level commit) if the purchasing entities can be listed on the PO and agree to joint billing. If Acme needs separate entity-level invoicing, we will need separate private offer addenda for each legal buyer — that increases administrative overhead but is straightforward.

Action items I propose: 
- Kimberly, can you draft a short appendix that outlines the escrow language and milestone release criteria (90-day onboarding milestones)?
- Marcus, can you confirm whether the 24-month discount schedule covers peak usage surges (we suggested a 15% headroom allowance in the projection file).

Maria/Jordan — if that model seems workable, we'll prepare a redline-ready doc and a DocuSign link for the named buyer entity. Trying to hit your 2028-07-26 buyer-approval cutoff.

Thanks,
Ben
